main_point: The failed NEWQ30 draft has real source omissions beyond a malformed raw checker: an unselected RuBP qualifier and stage context, missing per-unit reduction classification, an extra production-per-turn predicate, an uncited first summary sentence, and incoherent source ownership/unit selection in the final summary. No accepted or published final answer is available.
question: What happens to carbon fixed in the Calvin cycle: what does RuBisCO combine with CO2, how does the resulting compound become G3P, and why does some G3P leave while the rest remains?
method: Use the actual new submitted claim table, binding bank, syntactic-unit boundaries and 71 source fragments. Inspect exact lexical claim-object excerpts of the original invalid checker response separately, preserving its invalidity. No corrected whole model response or valid canonical selection is generated. Evaluate complete predicates, qualifications, context and summary locality rather than term overlap. The unvalidated apparent excerpts are evidence of model intent, not accepted selections.

source_coverage_and_science_boundaries: The qualified RuBP molecule requires actual F055; bare RuBP occurrences do not certify its carbon/phosphate qualifiers.
Actual F059 provides the explicit reduction relationship. An assessment of U01 using only F058 remains distinct from references assigned to another unit.
Actual F012 says each turn makes two G3Ps, but is in ev_002 outside the existing ev_001-only claim binding. Do not borrow it silently or infer a production rate from export wording.
Available source F025 has the old NADH anomaly, but it is not among the apparent selections reviewed here. No initial NADPH/NADH substitution was observed.
The first short sentence has no local marker. Body citations and the next summary sentence cannot backfill it.
Source text matching and favorable raw flags do not establish complete scientific direction, stoichiometry, conditions, or independent human certification.

available_candidates_not_actual_selected.exact_text: chloroplast has three carbon atoms, it takes three “turns” of the Calvin cycle to fix enough net carbon to export one G3P.
But each turn makes two G3Ps, thus three turns make six G3Ps.
One is exported while the remaining five G3P molecules remain in the cycle and are used to regenerate RuBP, which enables the system to prepare for more CO2 to be fixed.
The Calvin cycle reactions (Figure 5.15) can be organized into three basic stages: fixation, reduction, and regeneration.
In the stroma, in addition to CO2, two other chemicals are present to initiate the Calvin cycle: an enzyme abbreviated RuBisCO, and the molecule ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP).
RuBP has five atoms of carbon and a phosphate group on each end.
This type of reaction is called a reduction reaction, because it involves the gain of electrons.
